title: Chapter 7 Quiz
description: Test your knowledge of CSS basics, colours, typography, cascade, and inheritance!

questions.question: What does CSS stand for?
questions.explanation: CSS stands for Cascading Style Sheets.

questions.question: Which part of a CSS rule selects which elements to style?
questions.explanation: The selector targets the elements.

questions.question: What is the correct syntax for a class selector?
questions.explanation: A dot (.) precedes the class name.

questions.question: Inline styles are written inside a `<style>` block in the `<head>`.
questions.explanation: Inline styles are written directly in the `style` attribute of an element. A `<style>` block is internal CSS.

questions.question: Which tag links an external CSS file?
questions.explanation: <link rel="stylesheet" href="..."> loads an external stylesheet.

questions.question: What is the benefit of an external stylesheet?
options: It can be cached and reused across pages
questions.explanation: External files can be cached by the browser, improving performance and are reusable.

questions.question: Which colour format is `rgba(0, 0, 255, 0.5)`?
questions.explanation: RGBA defines red, green, blue, and alpha (transparency). 0,0,255 is blue; 0.5 is 50% opaque.

questions.question: What does `background-size: cover;` do?
options: Scales the image to fit entirely inside the element, leaving empty space
Stretches the image to the exact dimensions of the element
Scales the image to cover the entire element, cropping if necessary
questions.explanation: `cover` ensures the background covers the whole area, even if part of the image is cropped.

questions.question: Which property changes the text colour?
questions.explanation: The `color` property sets the foreground text colour.

questions.question: What is a generic font family that should end a font-family list?
questions.explanation: Generic families (serif, sans-serif, monospace) provide a fallback.

questions.question: How do you make text bold with CSS?
questions.explanation: `font-weight: bold;` or numeric values like 700.

questions.question: What does `line-height: 1.5;` mean?
questions.explanation: A unitless number multiplies the element's font size, making it scalable.

questions.question: Which property removes the underline from a link?
questions.explanation: `text-decoration: none;` is commonly used on `<a>` tags.

questions.question: If two rules have equal specificity, which one applies?
questions.explanation: When specificity is equal, the last rule in source order wins.

questions.question: `#main .title p` has higher specificity than `.title p`.
questions.explanation: #main adds an ID, increasing the specificity score.

questions.question: The CSS cascade considers origin, specificity, and ______ order.
questions.explanation: If specificity is equal, the last rule in the source code wins.

questions.question: Which of these properties is inherited by default?
questions.explanation: Text-related properties like `color`, `font-family` are inherited; box model properties are not.

questions.question: What does `!important` do in CSS?
options: It forces the declaration to override others regardless of specificity
questions.explanation: `!important` breaks the cascade and should be used sparingly.

questions.question: How can you force an element to inherit a non‑inherited property?
questions.explanation: The `inherit` keyword can be used as the value to force inheritance.

questions.question: What is the difference between `em` and `rem`?
options: `em` is relative to parent font size, `rem` is relative to root font size
questions.explanation: `em` cascades; `rem` is always relative to the `<html>` element's font size.

questions.question: Which CSS rule correctly applies a background image that doesn't repeat?
questions.explanation: You can use the shorthand `background` with `no-repeat` or separate properties.

questions.question: You can use the `@import` statement inside a `<style>` block to load an external CSS file.
questions.explanation: `@import url('styles.css');` works within a `<style>` tag or a CSS file, though `<link>` is preferred for performance.

questions.question: What does `text-transform: capitalize;` do?
options: Capitalises the first letter of each word
Capitalises the first letter of the first word
questions.explanation: `capitalize` transforms the first character of each word to uppercase.

questions.question: If the browser's default stylesheet makes `<h1>` 2em, and you set `h1 { font-size: 1.5em; }`, what happens?
options: The default is overridden because your stylesheet has higher origin priority
questions.explanation: Author stylesheets override browser defaults (user agent stylesheets).
